fiches.titre: ST2S-C-ANG01 · Taking a patient history in English
fiches.source: Programmes ST2S : arrete du 21 juillet 2011 fixant les programmes du baccalaureat technologique Sciences et technologies de la sante et du social (Bulletin officiel special n 6 du 29 septembre 2011) et programmes renoves applicables a la rentree 2020 (Bulletin officiel special n 7 du 25 juillet 2019) ; matieres : Droit et reglementation, Sante publique et environnement, Methodologie et Anglais professionnel de sante ; ressources eduscol ST2S. Textes officiels cites : Code de la sante publique, loi n 2002-303 du 4 mars 2002, reglement general sur la protection des donnees (reglement UE 2016/679).
points: Taking a patient history means collecting structured information about a person and their symptoms.
The interview usually starts with the chief complaint : the main reason for the consultation.
Open questions invite the patient to describe the problem in their own words.
Closed questions are useful to confirm a specific detail, such as the duration of a symptom.
The nurse or caregiver should introduce themselves and explain the purpose of the interview.
Confidentiality must be respected during the whole conversation.
The history includes personal details, current symptoms, past medical history and treatments.
Allergies and current medication are essential safety information.
The SOAPIER structure documents subjective data, objective data, assessment, plan, intervention, evaluation and revision.
Symptoms should be described with their location, intensity, duration, frequency and triggering factors.
The caregiver avoids medical jargon, checks understanding by asking the patient to repeat key points, and uses silence and active listening to encourage the patient to add important details.
The information is then recorded clearly and transmitted to the team.

questions.q: What is the chief complaint ?
options: The main reason for the consultation
questions.correction: The chief complaint is the main problem described by the patient.

questions.q: Which question is open ?
questions.correction: An open question cannot be answered by yes or no and invites description.

questions.q: What should the caregiver do first ?
options: Introduce themselves and explain the purpose
questions.correction: Introducing oneself and explaining the purpose builds trust and consent.

questions.q: Which information is essential for safety ?
questions.correction: Allergies and treatments must be known before any new intervention.

questions.q: What does the O stand for in SOAP ?
questions.correction: SOAP stands for Subjective, Objective, Assessment and Plan.

questions.q: How can understanding be checked ?
options: By asking the patient to repeat key points
questions.correction: Asking the patient to repeat verifies that the information was understood.

questions.q: How should symptoms be described ?
options: With location, intensity, duration and triggers
questions.correction: A complete description helps the team assess the problem accurately.

questions.q: Write five useful questions to explore a complaint of abdominal pain in English.
questions.reponse: Where exactly does the pain hurt ? When did it start ? How would you describe the pain, sharp or dull ? Does anything make it better or worse ? Have you taken any medicine for it ? These questions explore location, onset, character, modifying factors and treatment. They are open or semi-open and avoid suggesting the answer. The caregiver also asks about allergies and other symptoms such as nausea or fever, then records the answers using the patient's own words where possible.
questions.correction: Expected elements : location, onset, character, aggravating or relieving factors, medication.

questions.q: Explain why a caregiver should avoid medical jargon when taking a history.
questions.reponse: Medical terms such as dyspnoea or nausea may be unfamiliar to a patient, especially if English is not their first language. Using plain words gives a more accurate account of the symptoms. It also respects the person's autonomy : the patient understands what is happening and can give a valid consent. The caregiver can check comprehension by asking the patient to repeat the main points in their own words. Technical terms can still be recorded in the file, but the exchange itself must remain clear and respectful.
questions.correction: Expected elements : accuracy, comprehension, autonomy and verification of understanding.

affichage.texte: A good patient history is structured, respectful and clear : it turns the person's words into useful information.

fiches.titre: ST2S-C-ANG02 · Giving instructions, advice and dosage information
fiches.source: Programmes ST2S : arrete du 21 juillet 2011 fixant les programmes du baccalaureat technologique Sciences et technologies de la sante et du social (Bulletin officiel special n 6 du 29 septembre 2011) et programmes renoves applicables a la rentree 2020 (Bulletin officiel special n 7 du 25 juillet 2019) ; matieres : Droit et reglementation, Sante publique et environnement, Methodologie et Anglais professionnel de sante ; ressources eduscol ST2S. Textes officiels cites : Code de la sante publique, loi n 2002-303 du 4 mars 2002, reglement general sur la protection des donnees (reglement UE 2016/679).
points: Clear instructions help a patient use a treatment safely and correctly.
Take one tablet twice a day means one tablet in the morning and one in the evening.
Before meals, after meals and at bedtime are common timing expressions.
Swallow the tablet whole means that it must not be crushed or chewed.
Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol are frequent health recommendations.
Do not exceed the stated dose is a standard warning against overdose.
If you miss a dose, do not take a double dose : follow the leaflet or ask a professional.
Complete the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better.
Keep the medicine out of reach of children and store it as indicated on the box.
Side effects such as nausea or drowsiness should be reported if they persist.
The modal should gives advice, must expresses an obligation and may grants permission.
Instructions are easier to follow when they are short, ordered and confirmed by the patient ; the caregiver checks understanding and documents the information given.

questions.q: What does twice a day mean ?
questions.correction: Twice a day means two administrations in twenty-four hours.

questions.q: What does swallow the tablet whole mean ?
options: Do not crush or chew it
questions.correction: The tablet must be swallowed intact to preserve its formulation.

questions.q: Which modal expresses a strong obligation ?
questions.correction: Must expresses an obligation ; should expresses advice.

questions.q: What should a patient do after missing a dose ?
options: Follow the leaflet or ask a professional
questions.correction: Doubling a dose can be dangerous : the leaflet or a professional gives the rule.

questions.q: Why complete the full course of antibiotics ?
questions.correction: Stopping early can leave bacteria and favour resistance.

questions.q: What is a possible side effect ?
questions.correction: Nausea and drowsiness are examples of side effects.

questions.q: How should instructions be given ?
questions.correction: Short and ordered instructions, confirmed by the patient, are safer.

questions.q: Write clear instructions in English for a tablet to be taken twice a day with water, including warnings.
questions.reponse: Take one tablet twice a day, in the morning and in the evening, with a glass of water. Swallow the tablet whole : do not crush or chew it. Do not exceed the stated dose. If you miss a dose, do not take a double dose ; follow the leaflet or ask your nurse or pharmacist. If you feel nauseous or unusually sleepy, tell a healthcare professional. Keep the medicine out of reach of children. These sentences combine the dosage, the method, the warnings and the action in case of difficulty.
questions.correction: Expected elements : dosage, timing, water, do not crush, overdose warning, missed dose, side effects.

questions.q: Explain the difference between should and must when advising a patient.
questions.reponse: Should gives a recommendation : You should drink more water expresses advice that the patient is expected to follow but can discuss. Must expresses a requirement : You must not take this medicine with alcohol states a rule that must be respected for safety. In a care situation, choosing the wrong modal can make an essential instruction sound optional, or a simple suggestion sound like an order. The caregiver also checks that the patient has understood and can repeat the instruction before the treatment is given.
questions.correction: Expected elements : advice versus obligation, safety consequence and confirmation of understanding.

affichage.texte: Patient instructions must be short, precise and checked : dosage, timing, warnings and what to do in case of doubt.

affichage.leg: should = advice · must = obligation · may = permission

fiches.titre: ST2S-C-ANG03 · Medical terminology : roots, prefixes and suffixes
fiches.source: Programmes ST2S : arrete du 21 juillet 2011 fixant les programmes du baccalaureat technologique Sciences et technologies de la sante et du social (Bulletin officiel special n 6 du 29 septembre 2011) et programmes renoves applicables a la rentree 2020 (Bulletin officiel special n 7 du 25 juillet 2019) ; matieres : Droit et reglementation, Sante publique et environnement, Methodologie et Anglais professionnel de sante ; ressources eduscol ST2S. Textes officiels cites : Code de la sante publique, loi n 2002-303 du 4 mars 2002, reglement general sur la protection des donnees (reglement UE 2016/679).
points: Medical vocabulary is built from Greek and Latin word parts.
A root gives the main meaning, for example cardi for heart or pulmon for lung.
A prefix placed before the root modifies the meaning, such as hypo for low and hyper for high.
A suffix placed after the root also modifies the meaning, such as itis for inflammation and ology for study.
-ectomy means surgical removal, as in appendectomy, and -scopy means visual examination, as in endoscopy.
Hypoglycaemia means a low blood glucose level, while hyperglycaemia means a high level.
Hypertension means high blood pressure and hypotension means low blood pressure.
Tachycardia is a fast heart rate and bradycardia is a slow heart rate.
Dyspnoea means difficulty breathing and apnoea means absence of breathing.
Analgesia means absence of pain, while anaesthesia means loss of sensation.
Understanding word parts helps a caregiver decode an unfamiliar term in a file or a leaflet.
False friends exist : an Anglo-Saxon retreat is not a French retraite but a withdrawal or a side ward.

questions.q: What does the root cardi refer to ?
questions.correction: Cardi comes from the Greek kardia, meaning heart.

questions.q: What does the suffix itis mean ?
questions.correction: Appendicitis means inflammation of the appendix.

questions.q: What does hypo mean ?
questions.correction: Hypo indicates a low level, as in hypoglycaemia.

questions.q: What is tachycardia ?
questions.correction: Tachy means fast ; brady means slow.

questions.q: What does dyspnoea mean ?
questions.correction: Dys indicates difficulty ; pnoea refers to breathing.

questions.q: What does an appendectomy involve ?
questions.correction: The suffix ectomy means surgical removal.

questions.q: What does anaesthesia mean ?
questions.correction: Anaesthesia is loss of sensation ; analgesia is absence of pain.

questions.q: Decode the terms hypoglycaemia, hypertension and bronchoscopy using word parts.
questions.reponse: Hypoglycaemia combines hypo, meaning low, glycaem, referring to glucose in the blood, and the suffix ia, meaning condition : it is a low blood glucose level. Hypertension combines hyper, meaning high, and tension, referring to pressure : it means high blood pressure. Bronchoscopy combines broncho, referring to the bronchi, and scopy, meaning visual examination : it is an examination of the bronchi with an endoscope. Decomposing the word gives a reliable first meaning, which must then be checked against the clinical context.
questions.correction: Expected elements : hypo and hyper, root and suffix for each term, and the caution about context.

questions.q: Explain why medical roots and false friends matter for a French caregiver working in English.
questions.reponse: Knowing roots and affixes allows a caregiver to understand an unfamiliar term quickly, for example to recognise that a dermatology note concerns the skin or that an analgesia prescription concerns pain relief. False friends can cause the opposite effect : a word that looks French may have a different meaning in English, and a French medical term may not be the obvious translation. Misunderstanding a dosage or a symptom can affect safety. The caregiver therefore uses the word parts as a first clue, confirms with a dictionary or a colleague, and checks understanding with the patient.
questions.correction: Expected elements : decoding, false friends, safety and verification with reliable sources.

affichage.texte: Medical terms are built from roots, prefixes and suffixes : decoding them gives a first reliable meaning.

affichage.leg: ectomy = removal · scopy = examination · ology = study

fiches.source: Programmes ST2S : arrete du 21 juillet 2011 fixant les programmes du baccalaureat technologique Sciences et technologies de la sante et du social (Bulletin officiel special n 6 du 29 septembre 2011) et programmes renoves applicables a la rentree 2020 (Bulletin officiel special n 7 du 25 juillet 2019) ; matieres : Droit et reglementation, Sante publique et environnement, Methodologie et Anglais professionnel de sante ; ressources eduscol ST2S. points: Patient education helps a person understand their condition and participate in their care.
It starts by assessing what the patient already knows and what they want to know.
Information is given in small steps, with simple words and concrete examples.
The teach-back method asks the patient to explain the information in their own words.
Empathy means showing that the caregiver has understood the person's feelings without judging them.
Useful phrases include I can see this is difficult for you and Tell me how you feel about it.
Empathy is different from sympathy : the caregiver does not have to share the emotion to support the person.
Non-verbal communication includes eye contact, an open posture and an adapted distance, while silence can give the patient time to express a worry.
Encouragement should be sincere :You have made real progress is more useful than a vague compliment.
Shared decision-making presents options, benefits and risks, then respects the patient's choice.
Cultural and language differences require an interpreter when understanding is uncertain.
The caregiver documents the information given and checks the patient's understanding before the end.

questions.q: What is the teach-back method ?
options: Asking the patient to repeat the information in their own words
questions.correction: Teach-back verifies comprehension by asking the patient to explain the information back.

questions.q: Which phrase shows empathy ?
options: Do not worry, it is nothing
I can see this is difficult for you
questions.correction: This phrase recognises the feeling without minimising it.

questions.q: What does empathy involve ?
options: Understanding the person's feelings without judging
questions.correction: Empathy is understanding, not emotional fusion or sympathy.

questions.q: What does an adapted distance communicate ?
questions.correction: Distance and posture are part of non-verbal communication and respect for intimacy.

questions.q: When should an interpreter be used ?
options: When understanding is uncertain because of language or culture
questions.correction: An interpreter ensures that information is understood and consent is valid.

questions.q: What is sincere encouragement ?
options: A precise recognition of real progress
A promise that is not certain
questions.correction: Specific and truthful feedback is more useful than vague reassurance.

questions.q: What does shared decision-making require ?
options: Presenting options and respecting the patient's choice
questions.correction: It presents options, benefits and risks, then follows the person's informed choice.

questions.q: Write a short dialogue showing empathy when a patient says : I am afraid of the operation.
questions.reponse: Caregiver : I can see that you are afraid, and that is understandable. Patient : I had a bad experience before. Caregiver : Thank you for telling me. Tell me what worries you most about this operation. The caregiver keeps an open posture, respects a moment of silence and avoids saying there is nothing to fear. After listening, they explain the procedure step by step, use simple words and ask the patient to repeat the main points. They offer to involve the surgeon for further questions and document the concerns and the information given.
questions.correction: Expected elements : acknowledgement, open question, silence, simple information, teach-back and documentation.

questions.q: Explain the difference between empathy and sympathy in a caring relationship.
questions.reponse: Empathy means trying to understand the other person's experience and communicating that understanding, while keeping one's own emotional position. Sympathy means feeling with the person, which can create a strong emotional sharing and sometimes reduce professional distance. Both can be supportive, but empathy is more reliable in care because it keeps the caregiver able to act and decide. Showing empathy does not require saying I feel exactly what you feel ; it is enough to say I understand this is hard for you and to adapt the support to what the person needs.
questions.correction: Expected elements : understanding versus emotional sharing, professional distance and a concrete phrase.
